reading.rtitle: Stuck at the Airport? Know Your Rights
paras: Every winter, the same thing happens. A big snowstorm arrives in New York or Chicago, the airport announces a ground stop, and in a few hours there are hundreds of cancellations. Thousands of passengers are stranded, and the lines at the desks are hours long. You can't stop the snow, but you can stop the panic. The secret is to know your rights before you need them.

First, read the fine print of your ticket. It tells you what you are entitled to, and the answer depends on the cause. When the problem is beyond the airline's control, like the weather, most airlines will rebook you for free, but they usually do not pay for your hotel or your meals. When the cause is the airline's problem, like a broken plane or a missing crew, many airlines offer a meal voucher and a hotel. And in the United States, if the airline cancels your flight and you choose not to travel, you are entitled to a refund in money, not only a credit.

Second, act fast. Last winter, a traveler named Marta had a missed connection in Miami. She waited two hours in line, and when she got to the desk, the last flight was full. If she had called the airline from the gate, she would have gotten a seat that night. If she had asked for the waitlist, she would have had a chance. And if she had kept her taxi and hotel receipts, she would have received a reimbursement. Today, Marta files a claim online the same week, and she always asks the agent one simple question: "What are my options?"

listenings.text: Good evening, passengers on SkyAmerica Flight nine fifty-one to São Paulo. Because of the snowstorm, there is a ground stop for all departures from JFK, and this flight is now canceled. We are very sorry, but the weather is beyond our control. All passengers have been rebooked on tomorrow's flight at nine fifteen p.m. If you need an earlier flight, please ask an agent at gate twelve to put you on the waitlist for the morning flight at eight oh five. Because this cancellation is caused by weather, we are not able to offer hotel rooms tonight. However, if you choose not to travel, you are entitled to a full refund. Please check your email for all the details.

Last winter, a client called me from the airport in Chicago. Her flight was canceled, she was stranded, and she slept on the floor of the terminal. If she had called me first, I would have found her a hotel room in ten minutes. Here are three lessons from that night. First, don't just wait in the long line at the desk. While you wait, call the airline or use the app. The phone is often faster than the line. Second, keep every receipt: the taxi, the hotel, and the food. Without receipts, you can't file a claim for a reimbursement. Third, read the fine print before you travel. It tells you what you are entitled to. And remember: the agent at the desk didn't cause the snow. Be kind, and people will help you more.

extra_audio.text: First, I read the email from the airline and check the reason for the cancellation. Then, I call the airline while I wait in the line at the desk. Next, I ask the agent to put me on the waitlist for an earlier flight. After that, I book a hotel near the airport and keep every receipt. Finally, I file a claim online for a reimbursement.
